html: II. נכר (√ of foll., poss. = I. נכר, whence the foreign, strange, as that which is intently regarded, so Thes, but precarious; cf. Assyrian nakâru, rebel, Pa. change, nakiru, and nakaru, enemy, nukurtu, enmity, etc.; نَكِرَ in sense be bad, evil; be ignorant of, Qor 11:73; ii. change, alter, so as not to be known, disguise Qor 27:41; iv = i, also deny, Qor 16:85 repudiate.ii. change, alter a thing; Sab. נכר ii. reject, injure, etc., נכרם injury Sab Denkm76 CISiv. 81. 9; 29. 5; Min. נכר alter HomSüdarab. Chrest. 128; Syriac ܢܰܟܰܪ reject is rare (twice), and PS proposes ܢܘܽܟܪܳܝܳܐ alienus etc.; 𝔗 נוּכְרַי strange, foreign (proposes unknown, cf. Arabic √).).
